$comment: AsheFlow palette — THE source of truth (UI_UX_OVERHAUL_PLAN.md §3.1, §5 phase 0.1).
Web (frontend/src/index.css) and mobile (mobile/src/theme/index.ts) are both
GENERATED from this file by design/build_tokens.py. Do not hand-edit either.
They drifted before — web primary was #3C64DD, mobile #4F6BF4 — which is what
this file exists to prevent.
Every value carries its measured contrast in `_check`. design/check_contrast.py
re-measures and fails CI if any pairing regresses.
Colours are HSL triples because web CSS vars need that form; the generator
converts to hex for mobile.

$comment: Continuous gradient anchors for stop urgency (mobile stopUrgency.ts).
NOT semantic tokens. success/warning/danger are single values; this is a
SCALE that gets interpolated between, so it needs its own named anchors.
These were the last consumers of the legacy hardcoded `palette` export in
mobile/src/theme/index.ts, which shipped a second competing source of
truth (including #4F6BF4, the very value task 0.2 was meant to remove).
Theme-constant on purpose: the ramp encodes TIME PRESSURE, and a walker
reading it must get the same meaning from the same colour in either
theme. Contrast is not checked here because these are large fills behind
their own foreground, not text pairings.
Stored as HEX, not HSL: these are exact values carried over from the
legacy palette, and a hex->integer-HSL->hex round-trip shifted every one
of them by 1-2 per channel. Imperceptible, but it is silent corruption of
deliberate values. Theme-constant anchors gain nothing from HSL, which
exists so Tailwind can compose alpha.
their own foreground, not text pairings.
Colour-vision deficiency. success vs danger measured 1.05:1 under
deuteranopia (plan §2.3) — a walker could not tell delivered from failed.
MEASURED FINDING (2026-08-03): red / amber / green CANNOT be separated by
colour choice under deuteranopia. All three collapse toward yellow, so only
LIGHTNESS separates them, and reaching even 1.6:1 needs ~25-30 lightness
points — at which point success is a pale mint or danger a washed pink and
neither reads as its own semantic colour. Degrading the palette to chase a
threshold that still would not make colour safe is the wrong trade.
So: the red/amber/green cluster is ADVISORY (reported, never fails). Its
real mitigation is plan §4 rule 1 — every status carries an icon or label,
enforced by the primitive API in phase 2, not by the palette.
ENFORCED pairs are those where separation IS achievable: the interactive
accent must never be mistaken for a status colour, which is the whole
reason brand moved off amber (plan §2.4).

enforced.$metric: Perceptual distance in Lab under simulated CVD, NOT contrast ratio. Contrast is luminance-only and cannot see hue: it scores violet (#4D4DD2 under deuteranopia) against olive (#6F6F01) at 1.09:1 despite them being obviously different colours. 25 = comfortably distinguishable.

brand-vs-primary-dark: Cause: on a dark navy background BOTH must be lifted to stay readable,
and lifting pushes them together. Full hue-space search found the only
way to clear 25 is a pink/magenta accent (#F42A6D, distance 50.4),
which abandons violet and desynchronises light from dark.
Accepted because the collision is accent-vs-BRAND, not accent-vs-STATUS.
